title: Relationships We (Mostly) Choose: Setting Boundaries with Friends and Neighbors
coreMove: Friend and neighbor boundaries protect chosen-relationship capacity by naming what access is welcome, what support is available, and where time, space, or bandwidth ends.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who become the default listener for one friend
exampleSpecs.stakes: Unlimited listening can turn care into depletion and private resentment.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Limit emotional dumping while leaving a smaller, honest opening for care.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose private routines have become public by proximity
exampleSpecs.stakes: A kind neighbor can still take over the only quiet part of the day.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Preserve weekday solitude by offering a weekend form of connection.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers sharing housing with someone they care about
exampleSpecs.stakes: Sobriety, sleep, food routines, and guests can become daily stress without explicit rules.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Treat shared-space limits as practical infrastructure, not emotional rejection.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who invent excuses when their calendar is technically open
exampleSpecs.stakes: False reasons invite negotiation and teach friends to solve the wrong problem.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use chosen-relationship capacity as the reason instead of a fabricated conflict.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who want to redirect a friend without rejection
exampleSpecs.stakes: A friend may need more support than one listener can safely provide.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ask permission before venting and redirect emotional dumping toward a wider support structure.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose friendly availability has become assumed access
exampleSpecs.stakes: Home routines can be overrun when every visible light or open door is treated as an invitation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn a friendly neighbor pattern into a clear request for notice before visits.
